annotations.text:
F · Fastgraph

Same tokens as DMS Fastgraph's default dark theme: window #07090C, panels #121820 with 12 px radius, borders #334152, Inter + Inconsolata, accent #66CCFF. Buttons are the Fastgraph recessed-well button with the radial glow that rises on hover. Segmented Start/Top/End control, pill toggles, spin fields, plot with dashed grid and axis titles, status bar.

Tweak: the accent chip swaps blue for DMS yellow.

Tradeoff: densest of all rounds; reads as an app window rather than a page.

D · Quiet, light

One grotesk, one mono, hairlines, no boxes. Warm off-white so it reads as paper, not a web app. Yellow only where it means something: the curve, the current band, Copy.

Tradeoff: a light page next to a dark music player or DAW can feel bright during a long session.

E · Quiet, dark

Same design on neutral near-black. Easier on the eyes for long sweeps and the yellow curve carries more.

Tradeoff: dark plus thin hairlines needs care on cheap displays; gray text contrast is the thing to watch.

A · Bench instrument

Why: reads as a piece of test gear you trust. Engraved labels, a tape-style tuner, lamps. The tone readout is the hero.

Tradeoff: skeuomorphic details (knob, lamps) need restraint or they tip into kitsch. Densest of the three.

B · Lab notebook

Why: warmest and most human. Layered paper sheets, serif display type, pencil-style marks on graph paper. Feels like your own notes, not a product.

Tradeoff: least 'tool-like'; some users may read it as less precise. Grain and paper edges must stay subtle.

C · Broadcast console

Why: maximum contrast and clarity. Raised black modules, amber readouts, a big STOP. Fastest to scan while sweeping.

Tradeoff: the coldest of the three and closest to a generic pro-audio look; character comes from restraint and the amber-only palette.
